$comment: Stable identifiers shared by the Android and iOS SDKs and the Flutter and React Native adapters. Values may be added in a minor contract version; they are never renamed, removed or given a different meaning.

errorCodes.meaning: The request did not reach the server, or a read failed on the network.
A read-only request timed out. Never used for mutating requests (see outcome_unknown).
HTTP 429. The caller must wait before trying again.
TLS could not be established or the certificate was rejected.
HTTP 5xx answered to a read-only request.
The session provider failed or returned an unusable session.
The access token was rejected (HTTP 401 or 403) after the allowed refresh.
Payment channels could not be loaded.
A read-only response could not be understood.
The API rejected the transaction request payload (HTTP 400 or 422).
The transaction is unknown to the API.
The transaction definitely did not succeed (failure, fraud, expired, refunded) or creation was definitively refused.
The BLIK code was rejected or is no longer usable.
A mutating request may or may not have taken effect. Never repeated automatically; reconcile by control from webhooks.
The order failed local validation. Nothing was sent.
Neither the session nor the order supplied the payer IP. Nothing was sent.
No customer country was given and the currency maps to no single country. Nothing was sent.
A checkout is already on screen. The new call is answered at once.
The payment sheet could not be shown. No transaction was attempted.
Invalid configuration or unsupported bridge payload version. Nothing was sent.
No browser can open the payment page (Android only).
Unexpected failure inside the SDK.

pendingReasons.meaning: The last known status is new, generated or confirmed.
transaction_fraud_possibility: the transaction is under verification.
The API returned a status this contract version does not know. Never a success.
The status could not be read, or was not read before the checkout closed.

resultTypes.meaning: The API reported transaction_paid. Not proof of payment; the merchant backend confirms from the webhook.
A transaction exists; its final outcome is not known yet. Never a failure.
The payment definitely did not succeed, or the checkout failed before any transaction could have been created.
It is unknown whether a transaction was created. Never repeated automatically.
The payer left before any transaction was requested.
